label: Accolade type
summary: Whether the accolade is of the given type.
details: Vanilla uses it with types such as `lancer_attribute`, `horse_archer_attribute` and `outrider_attribute`.

label: Has active diarchy
summary: Whether the character has a diarchy that is currently active.
details: Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Locale is active
summary: Whether the activity currently has the given locale active.
details: Works on an activity. Vanilla uses it with the tournament locales, such as `tournament_locale_artisans` and `tournament_locale_tavern`.

label: Has active mandate
summary: Whether the diarch (the character it runs on) has the given mandate active.
details: The game's documentation shows it run inside `scope:diarch = { ... }`. Vanilla uses mandates such as `promote_might`, `promote_merit` and `fill_coffers`.

label: Has activity intent
summary: Whether the character has the given activity intent.
details: Vanilla uses intents such as `woo_attendee_intent`, `murder_attendee_intent` and `befriend_attendee_intent`.

label: Activity option chosen
summary: Whether the activity has the given option active in the given option category.
details: Both parts are needed: the category names the choice group, the option names the pick inside it. Vanilla mostly checks the category `special_type` with options like `hunt_type_falconry` or `tour_type_majesty`.

fields.name: category
fields.text: The group of options the choice belongs to.
fields.values: a category key, such as `special_type` or `feast_option_food`

fields.name: option
fields.text: The option that must be active in that category.

label: Activity state
summary: Whether the character's current activity is in the given state.
details: The states are `travel`, `passive` and `active`. It looks at the activity the character is involved in right now.

label: Activity type
summary: Whether the activity is of the given type.
details: Vanilla uses types such as `activity_wedding`, `activity_feast`, `activity_hunt` and `activity_pilgrimage`.

label: Has all innovations
summary: Whether the culture has discovered every innovation that matches the filter.
details: All three filter lines are optional; each one narrows which innovations count. Vanilla does not use it in the input, so the details rest on the game's documentation.

fields.name: with_flag
fields.text: Only innovations that carry this flag count.

fields.name: without_flag
fields.text: Only innovations that do not carry this flag count.

fields.name: culture_era
fields.text: Only innovations from this era count.

label: Has all variables
summary: Whether the current object has every one of the listed variables set.
details: Write one `name = ...` line per variable. It is true only when all of them exist. The game's documentation names no fixed type it runs on.

fields.name: name
fields.text: A variable that must be set. Repeat the line for more variables.

label: Gender allowed as clergy
summary: Whether the target character has a gender that the faith allows for its clergy.
details: Runs on a faith; the character to check is the value you write.

label: Has any artifact
summary: Whether the character has at least one artifact.
details: Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Has any artifact claim
summary: Whether the character has a claim on any artifact at all.
details: The game's documentation marks it as cheap to run. Write `yes` or `no`. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Has any casus belli on
summary: Whether the character has any casus belli (a valid reason for war) against the target character.
details: The character to check against is the value you write, for example `scope:recipient`.

label: Has any court position
summary: Whether the character holds at least one court position.
details: Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Has displayed casus belli on
summary: Whether the character has any casus belli against the target character that should be displayed.
details: Like the plain casus belli check, but it only counts those meant to be displayed. The game's documentation adds that such a casus belli is allowed to fail the check named `valid_to_start_display_regardless`.

label: Has a focus
summary: Whether the character has any focus set.
details: Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Has a nickname
summary: Whether the character has any nickname.
details: Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Has opinion with reason
summary: Whether the character holds an opinion of anyone that was given for the named reason.
details: The documented example uses `imprisonment_reason`. Vanilla does not use it in the input, so which reason keys are valid is not shown.

label: Has any scripted relation with
summary: Whether the character has any scripted relation with the target character.
details: The character to check against is the value you write.

label: Has any secret relation with
summary: Whether the character has any secret relation with the target character.
details: The character to check against is the value you write. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Has any secrets
summary: Whether the character has any secrets.
details: Write `yes` or `no`. Vanilla only ever writes `yes`.

label: Has unequipped artifact
summary: Whether the character has at least one artifact that is not equipped.
details: Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Influence level for appointment
summary: Whether the character has a high enough Influence Level for an appointment to the target title.
details: It ignores the title laws currently in force. The title to check is the value you write, for example `scope:target_title`. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Investor backs character
summary: Whether the character (the investor) has supported the appointment of the target character in the same realm.
details: It does not matter whether the candidate already has a valid reason to be appointed. The documented example names a different key (`has_appointment_investment_in_character`) than this one.

label: Investor backs title
summary: Whether the character (the investor) has supported an appointment to the target title in the same realm.
details: It stays true even when the candidate has died; the game's documentation says this is for efficiency. The documented example names a different key (`has_appointment_investment_in_title`) than this one. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Appointment level for title
summary: Whether the character has a currency level that is enough for an appointment to the target title.
details: The title is the value you write. Vanilla passes titles such as `scope:target` and `scope:title`. The game's documentation does not say which currency is meant, so only the general meaning is known.

label: Merit level for appointment
summary: Whether the character has a high enough Merit Level for an appointment to the target title.
details: It ignores the title laws currently in force. The title to check is the value you write. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Piety level for appointment
summary: Whether the character has a high enough Level of Devotion for an appointment to the target title.
details: It ignores the title laws currently in force. The title to check is the value you write. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Prestige level for appointment
summary: Whether the character has a high enough Prestige Level for an appointment to the target title.
details: It ignores the title laws currently in force. The title to check is the value you write. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Has artifact claim
summary: Whether the character has a personal or house claim on the target artifact.
details: The artifact is the value you write, often `prev` or a saved scope.

label: Artifact feature
summary: Whether the artifact has the given feature.
details: Vanilla uses it a lot, mostly with book subjects such as `book_subject_learning` and `book_subject_diplomacy`.

label: Artifact feature group
summary: Whether the artifact has the given feature group.
details: Vanilla uses groups such as `decoration_material_inlay`, `decoration_material_gem` and `generic_material_wood`.

label: Artifact modifier
summary: Whether the artifact has the given artifact modifier.
details: Vanilla uses it with modifiers such as `double_moon_modifier` and `pam_chrismated_artifact_modifier`.

label: Tenet status at least
summary: Whether the rite holds at least the given stance on the given tenet.
details: A stronger stance also passes. The order is: unknown, then known, then permitted, then core; and unknown, then known, then prohibited. Rites only override the faith's core tenets, and the faith's core tenets count as permitted for the rite.

label: Has hostages abroad
summary: Whether the character has hostages abroad.
details: Write `yes` or `no`. Vanilla does not use it in the input.

label: Has bad nickname
summary: Whether the character has a nickname that counts as bad.
details: Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Has banish reason
summary: Whether the character has a banish reason towards the target character.
details: The target character is the value you write, for example `scope:recipient` or `root`.

label: House base name
summary: Whether the house has the given base name.
details: Works on a house. A lowborn character has no house, so check for a house first, as in the documented example `house ?= { has_base_name = ... }`. The documented example writes the name as a quoted key.

label: Has building
summary: Whether the province has the given building.
details: Vanilla uses it with keys such as `temple_01`, `temple_02` and `legendary_shrine`.
